about: How read-data/skills-into-workflows.mjs turns a person's own agent skills (rows of their agent-skills list, each file in parts) into workflows in their own account. One skill becomes one workflow: its instructions are the one step's do, and its text files ride along under files. Ported from old Trillion's records/skill-import-rules.json (scripts/skills-to-workflows.mjs, src/skill-rows.mjs, commit 99651cea06). The rows go only into the person's own account, so the old sharing rule (a skill ships only when its maker may share it) is not a gate here; the licence a skill declares rides on the row's source. A skill stays home when any text that would ship matches a never_share pattern or one of the person's private words. Changing what is screened is a row here, never a change to the script.

author_words.comment: A licence's copyright line names who holds it: 'Copyright (c) 2026 Some Name' reads 'Some Name'. A skill's own front-matter author wins over this.

budget.comment: describe_workflow returns a row whole, so a skill's row stays under max_row_characters. Its SKILL.md always goes in; text files beside it go in, smallest first, while they fit; the rest are named under files_left_out.

never_share.says: holds what looks like a secret key or token
names a folder on one person's computer

never_share.comment: An address whose domain has an example label (RFC 2606 example.com, example.org, example.net, or any sub.example.co.uk), or a one-letter name at a one-letter domain (a, the at sign, b.co), is an illustration, never a real person's.
